Hi Katie — thanks for sending these over and for the certificate.

Quick answers up front:
- We can support split-entity invoicing but it typically needs a brief accounting runbook and a billing schedule in the Order Form so finance knows which entity takes which tranche.
- Splitting the minimum commit across entities is possible but there are two impacts to flag: 1) pricing bands and volume discounts are evaluated at the invoice-entity level in our billing engine; splitting can therefore change the effective blended price unless the Order Form explicitly pools the commit across entities, and 2) the MSA currently ties remedies/credits to the consolidated commit; an amendment may be required depending on how Momentum wants crediting handled.

I'm looping in Camila (AE) and Kimberly (Finance) to confirm what we can do without an MSA amendment and to scope any operational steps. I've attached a short summary of the redlines we received (redlines_summary_sergio.docx).

Can we do a 30-minute sync Thursday 11:00 AM PT? If that works I can send a calendar invite and draft an Order Form delta that includes split-entity billing language and a pooled-commit clause to preserve discounts.

Hi team — reviewed Momentum's redlines and tax cert. Operational comments:

1) Split-entity invoicing: Redwood Finance can support issuing invoices from different legal entities, but we need the following:
   - A signed intercompany billing runbook specifying invoice entity for each tranche (we typically add this as an appendix to the Order Form).
   - A W-8/W-9 or local tax evidence for each Momentum entity to satisfy our withholding and VAT obligations.

2) Pooled commit for discounts: Finance is OK with the pooled-commit approach if Momentum signs an amendment stating that (a) the parties agree to aggregate committed units for purposes of pricing band calculation only, and (b) invoicing/collections will follow the specified invoice entity per tranche. This keeps legal remedies tied to the MSA but preserves commercial economics.

3) Net terms: Momentum requested Net 45 in their redlines. Our standard for new customers is Net 30. If Momentum needs Net 45, we can accommodate that under two conditions: (i) Treasury approval of credit terms (Ben will route a quick risk assessment), or (ii) Momentum provides an upfront guarantee (letter of credit or advance payment for the first tranche).

I've attached a sample billing appendix template and a checklist (billing_appendix_template.pdf). I'll also add a short tax evidence checklist to the Doc we circulate.

Kimberly Park
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: billing_appendix_template.pdf
